category: Acoustics Module III: ray acoustics, acoustic diffusion, acoustic multiphysics couplings, acoustics studies and postprocessing
description: Geometrical acoustics (Ray Acoustics features, receivers, impulse response and room-acoustic metrics; Acoustic Diffusion Equation), every acoustics multiphysics coupling (structure, thermoviscous, porous, aeroacoustic, BEM-FEM, pipe, time explicit, streaming, piezo transducers), acoustics-specific study steps and results tools (octave band, directivity, SPL/intensity/transmission-loss variables). Coupling type strings and default tags were read from the COMSOL 6.4 multiphysics plugin definitions and Application Library models.

tools.name: Medium Properties (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Default domain node of Ray Acoustics (rac) that defines the speed of sound, density and bulk attenuation of the propagation medium. Fluid models are Linear elastic, User-defined attenuation, Atmosphere attenuation (humidity and temperature dependent, ANSI S1.26), Ocean attenuation and Thermally conducting and viscous; attenuation matters for large halls, outdoor propagation and high frequencies. For unmeshed domains, material data is set under Material Properties of Exterior and Unmeshed Domains at the interface level.
tools.usage: Ray Acoustics > Medium Properties 1 (mp1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").feature("mp1").set("FluidModel", "Atmosphere")

parameters.name: FluidModel
parameters.description: LinearElastic | Attenuation | Atmosphere | Ocean | Viscothermal.

parameters.name: c, rho
parameters.description: Speed of sound and density (From material or user defined).

parameters.name: AttenuationType, alpha1, alpha1m, alpha2, alpha3
parameters.description: Amplitude (Np/m, dB/m, dB/wavelength) or intensity attenuation coefficient m.

parameters.name: Model inputs T, pA, relative humidity
parameters.description: Used by the atmosphere model; pH for ocean.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Attenuation is only evaluated when ray intensity or power is computed (Intensity Computation setting of the interface).

tools.name: Release from Point (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Releases rays from selected geometry points with a spherical, hemispherical, conical or user-defined direction distribution, the standard omnidirectional point source of room and outdoor acoustics. Settings include the number of rays in wave-vector space, total source power, initial phase and intensity, ray frequency (or a frequency distribution) and optional multiple release times. For directional sources use Source with Directivity; for many points from a grid use Release from Grid.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Release from Point (rpt1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("rpt1", "ReleaseFromPoint", 0)

parameters.name: RayDirectionVector
parameters.description: Spherical | Hemispherical | Conical | Expression (with L0, rax, cax, alphac).

parameters.name: Nw
parameters.description: Number of rays in wave vector space.

parameters.name: Psrc
parameters.description: Total source power.

parameters.name: f0, FDistributionFunction
parameters.description: Initial ray frequency or a frequency distribution when enabled at the interface level.

parameters.name: rt / TimeDistributionFunction
parameters.description: Release times (with Allow multiple release times).

tools.notes: In 2D axisymmetry use Release from Point on Axis. Ray count needed for a converged impulse response depends on room volume and receiver radius (see Impulse Response).

tools.name: Release from Boundary (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Releases rays from interior or exterior boundaries, for example a vibrating panel, a window, or a loudspeaker baffle, with positions based on the mesh, a density expression or a projected plane grid and directions given as a vector, hemispherical, conical or Lambertian-type distribution. The wavefront shape can follow the surface curvature or be a plane/cylindrical wave, and the total source power can be distributed uniformly or weighted. A Nonlocal Accumulator subnode can send ray information back to the release boundary.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Release from Boundary (relb1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("relb1", "ReleaseFromBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: InitialPosition, Nr
parameters.description: Mesh based | Density | ProjectedPlaneGrid positions and the number of rays per release.

parameters.name: RayDirectionVector, Nw, alphac, cax, rax
parameters.description: Direction distribution and number of rays in wave-vector space.

parameters.name: Psrc, InitialPowerDistribution, Pwt
parameters.description: Total source power and uniform or weighted distribution.

parameters.name: WavefrontShape
parameters.description: FromSurfaceCurvature | PlaneWave | CylindricalWave.

tools.notes: Release from Edge and Release from Data File cover edge sources and fully tabulated ray starts.

tools.name: Release from Edge / Release from Data File (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Two additional ray sources. Release from Edge launches rays from positions along 3D edges (mesh based, uniform distribution of N rays or density), useful for line-like sources such as road or rail segments. Release from Data File reads initial positions, directions, frequencies and auxiliary variables from a spreadsheet-style text file (one ray per row, '%' comments), e.g. rays exported from measurements or another simulation.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Release from Edge (redg1) / Release from Data File (relf1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("redg1", "ReleaseFromEdge", 1); create("relf1", "ReleaseFromDataFile", -1)

parameters.name: Initial position (edge)
parameters.description: Mesh based | Uniform distribution (N rays) | Density.

parameters.name: Filename, icolp, icold, icolf
parameters.description: Data file and column indices of position, direction and frequency data.

parameters.name: RayDirectionVector
parameters.description: FromFile | Expression | Spherical | Hemispherical | Conical for the file release.

parameters.name: Psrc, I0, Psi0
parameters.description: Power, initial intensity and phase.

tools.notes: The -1 (global) dimension for ReleaseFromDataFile is an assumption based on it having no geometric selection; verify by saving a GUI-built model as Java.

tools.name: Release from Exterior Field Calculation (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: 3D multiscale source that launches rays whose initial intensity and phase follow the far field of a Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain near-field model (Exterior Field Calculation with the far-field integral approximation). It transfers a detailed loudspeaker or transducer radiation pattern, including baffle diffraction, into a ray model of a room or vehicle; the ray frequency is locked to the source study frequency.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Release from Exterior Field Calculation (rext1); reference the efc variable from the pressure acoustics study. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("rext1", "ReleaseFromExteriorFieldCalculation", -1)

parameters.name: ExtName
parameters.description: Exterior field variable (e.g. the efc1 pext variable of acpr).

parameters.name: x0, Ealpha/Ebeta/Egamma
parameters.description: Source location and orientation (Z-X-Z Euler angles).

parameters.name: RayDirectionVector, Nw, HemisphereAxis, ConeAxis
parameters.description: Spherical | Hemispherical | Conical distribution and number of rays.

parameters.name: GridType
parameters.description: AllCombinations | SpecifiedCombinations of release parameters.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module; 3D only and intensity or power must be computed. The near-field model must resolve waves (about 5 second-order elements per wavelength). The global dimension -1 is assumed.

tools.name: Release from Pressure Field (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Creates realistic ray sources from a wave-based (near-field) Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain submodel: rays are released from the radiating boundaries of that submodel in the direction of the local acoustic intensity and with power weighted by it. This captures local reflections and diffraction around a source installed in a complex setting (e.g. a loudspeaker in a car dashboard) that plain ray point sources cannot represent.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Release from Pressure Field (rpf1) on the boundaries of the pressure acoustics submodel. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("rpf1", "ReleaseFromPressureField", 2)

parameters.name: Pressure acoustics source
parameters.description: The Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain interface/solution that provides the field.

parameters.name: Ray release density / number of rays
parameters.description: Controls how many rays are launched from the boundaries.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Radiating boundaries of the near-field submodel.

tools.notes: Available when Compute power, Compute intensity or Compute intensity and power is selected. The ray frequency is locked to the pressure acoustics frequency. Setting names are not listed in the completion data summary; set them in the GUI.

tools.name: Source with Directivity (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: 3D point source that releases rays in a spherical or hemispherical distribution with initial power following a spatial directivity function of the polar and azimuthal angles (rac.swd1.theta, rac.swd1.phi), for loudspeakers and human talkers in room acoustics. Directivity can be given as an SPL at a reference distance (e.g. measured balloon data via an interpolation function of angles and band frequency) or by the total source power; a local coordinate system orients the source.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Source with Directivity (swd1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("swd1", "SourceWithDirectivity", -1)

parameters.name: q0
parameters.description: Source location.

parameters.name: Directivity
parameters.description: SpecifySpatialDirectivity | SpecifyTotalSourcePower.

parameters.name: D, Lref, Rref
parameters.description: Spatial directivity (dB) and reference SPL at reference distance.

parameters.name: Psrc, Nw, RayDirectionVector
parameters.description: Total power, number of rays and Spherical | Hemispherical distribution.

parameters.name: coordinateSystem, SpecifyLocalCoordinates, ef, et
parameters.description: Source orientation.

tools.notes: 3D only. A radiation balloon computed in pressure acoustics can be exported with Results > Export > Radiation Pattern (type RadiationPattern) and reused as directivity data. The global dimension -1 matches a feature with a coordinate-based location (q0).

tools.name: Wall (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Default ray-acoustics boundary condition for walls, absorbers, diffusers and sea beds. The default Mixed diffuse and specular reflection uses a scattering coefficient s (Lambertian vs specular split) and an absorption coefficient alpha, both typically band-frequency dependent via interpolation functions; alternatives are Specular reflection or Freeze. The reflection coefficient can also come from an impedance, fluid-fluid or fluid-solid interface, or layered half-space model, and Rayleigh surface roughness is optional.
tools.usage: Ray Acoustics > Wall 1 (wall1, default) or right-click > Wall. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("wall2", "RayAcousticsWall", 2)

parameters.name: WallCondition
parameters.description: MixedDiffuseSpecular (default) | SpecularReflection | Freeze.

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: Scattering coefficient (0.05 typical for flat surfaces).

parameters.name: ComputeReflectedIntensityUsing
parameters.description: AbsorptionCoefficient | AbsorberSpecifiedImpedance | ReflectionCoefficient | FluidFluidInterface | FluidSolidInterface | LayeredFluidHalfSpace.

parameters.name: alpha, R, Z1
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient, reflection coefficient or absorber impedance.

parameters.name: UseRayleighSurfaceRoughness, sigmar
parameters.description: Rayleigh roughness with RMS roughness.

tools.notes: Use the random-incidence absorption coefficients per octave band. A Wall with Pass through (General Wall) on a meshed interior plane can be used to map SPL in a cross section.

tools.name: General Wall (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Advanced ray wall with all interaction options: Freeze, Specular reflection, Stick, Disappear, Pass through, Diffuse scattering, Isotropic scattering, Mixed diffuse and specular reflection, and General reflection with a user-defined reflected direction. Conditions can be restricted by a probability or logical expression (with an Otherwise fallback), separate specular and diffuse absorption/reflection/impedance can be defined, and manual phase shifts or Rayleigh roughness applied.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > General Wall (gwall1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("gwall1", "GeneralWall", 2)

parameters.name: WallCondition
parameters.description: Freeze | Stick | Disappear | Pass | SpecularReflection | DiffuseScattering | IsotropicScattering | MixedDiffuseSpecular | GeneralReflection.

parameters.name: PrimaryRayCondition, gamma, e, Otherwise
parameters.description: NoneCondition | Probability | Expression and the fallback condition.

parameters.name: gammas, alphas, alphad, Rs, Rd, Z1s, Z1d
parameters.description: Specular probability and separate specular/diffuse absorption, reflection or impedance.

parameters.name: Lprim
parameters.description: Reflected ray direction for General reflection.

parameters.name: SurfaceRoughnessModel, sigmar
parameters.description: NoneSurfaceRoughness | RayleighRoughness.

tools.notes: Disappear is typical for openings; Pass through for measurement planes.

tools.name: Receiver (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: 3D feature applied to the surface of a receiver sphere (a surface-type geometry object, meshed at about R/3) that records arrival time, power and direction of every ray crossing it, without affecting ray propagation. The data feed the Receiver 3D dataset and the Impulse Response plot. The receiver radius can be automatic or user defined, and an omnidirectional or user-defined directivity (e.g. of a microphone or a binaural head) can be assigned.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Receiver (rec1) on the receiver sphere boundaries; requires Compute power (or intensity and power) and Count reflections. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("rec1", "Receiver", 2)

parameters.name: ReceiverRadius, rrec
parameters.description: Automatic | UserDefined receiver radius (0.3 m typical for a seat).

parameters.name: DirectivityType
parameters.description: Omnidirectional | UserDefinedLogarithmic | UserDefinedLinear.

parameters.name: D, dir, coordinateSystem
parameters.description: Directivity expression in dB (or linear) and orientation.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module; 3D only. The number of rays N needed for a 1 dB error per 10 ms depends on room volume and receiver radius (formula in the Impulse Response section).

tools.name: Ray Detector (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Counts rays located in selected domains or on selected boundaries, optionally only those from a given release feature, and defines the number of transmitted rays, the transmission probability, a logical filter expression for rendering, and (when power is solved) the total transmitted power as a global variable. It is used to evaluate how much energy reaches an opening, a seating area or a target surface.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Ray Detector (rd1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("rd1", "RayDetector", 2)

parameters.name: ReleaseFeature
parameters.description: All (default) or a specific release feature.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Detector domains or boundaries.

tools.notes: See 'Using Ray Detectors' in the modeling section for variable names.

tools.name: Sound Pressure Level Calculation (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Subnode of Wall (available when ray power is solved) that computes the sound pressure level on the wall from the incident and reflected rays, giving surface SPL maps of rooms, audience planes or building facades. An optional smoothing radius defines smoothed intensity and SPL variables (e.g. rac.wall1.spl1.Iw_sm, rac.wall1.spl1.Lp_sm) that reduce ray noise.
tools.usage: Right-click Wall (Ray Acoustics) > Sound Pressure Level Calculation (spl1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").feature("wall1").create("spl1", "SoundPressureLevelBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: ComputeSmoothedAccumulatedVariable
parameters.description: Enable smoothed variables.

parameters.name: rsm
parameters.description: Smoothing radius (m).

tools.notes: For an SPL map in free space add a meshed interior plane with a General Wall set to Pass through and this subnode.

tools.name: Accumulator / Nonlocal Accumulator (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Features that transfer ray information to the mesh. The domain Accumulator and the boundary Accumulator (Wall subnode) define an accumulated variable per mesh element from a source term R summed over rays (as Density or Count, over elements or elements and time), e.g. absorbed energy or ray counts for heating or dose maps. The Nonlocal Accumulator (Release from Boundary subnode) communicates information from where a ray currently is back to its release position, e.g. for view-factor or transmission computations.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Accumulator (dacc1); right-click Wall > Accumulator (Boundary); right-click Release from Boundary > Nonlocal Accumulator. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("dacc1", "DomainAccumulator", 3)

parameters.name: AccumulatorType
parameters.description: Density | Count.

parameters.name: AccumulateOver
parameters.description: Elements | ElementsAndTime.

parameters.name: R, AccumulatedVariableName, DependentVariableQuantity
parameters.description: Source term, variable name and physical quantity/unit.

parameters.name: ReleaseFeature, SourceInterpolation
parameters.description: Restrict to rays of one release; Constant/Linear/Quadratic/Exponential interpolation of the source.

tools.notes: Accumulated variables add degrees of freedom on the mesh; keep the mesh moderately coarse.

tools.name: Ray Termination (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Removes rays that leave the geometry bounding box (from geometry, user defined or none) and, when intensity or power is computed, rays whose intensity or power falls below a threshold. For room acoustics the recommended setting is Bounding box, from geometry plus a Power criterion with threshold P0/N*1e-6 (a 60 dB drop for an omnidirectional source), which keeps the ray count and solution time under control.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Ray Termination (rt1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("rt1", "RayTermination", -1)

parameters.name: SpatialExtentsOfRayPropagation
parameters.description: BoundingBoxFromGeometry | BoundingBoxUserDefined (xmin..zmax) | NoneSpatialExtents.

parameters.name: AdditionalTerminationCriteria
parameters.description: NoneTerminationCriteria | Power (and intensity when computed).

parameters.name: Qth, Ith
parameters.description: Threshold power or intensity.

tools.notes: Only one Ray Termination node per interface. The global dimension -1 is assumed (no selection).

tools.name: Ray Properties (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Singleton default node that defines the ray propagation equations and the ray frequency when frequency distributions at release features are not enabled. In room acoustics the ray frequency is set to the parameter holding the octave or third-octave band center frequency (e.g. f0), which is then swept in a Parametric Sweep around the Ray Tracing study so that absorption, scattering, source power and air attenuation are evaluated per band.
tools.usage: Ray Acoustics > Ray Properties 1 (op1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").feature("op1").set("f", "f0")

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Ray frequency (default 1000 Hz); locked to the source frequency when Release from Pressure Field or Exterior Field Calculation is used.

tools.notes: For the Impulse Response plot only enter 0 and the final time in the Ray Tracing times list.

tools.name: Background Velocity / Material Discontinuity (Ray Acoustics)
tools.description: Background Velocity assigns a flow velocity field to the medium (e.g. wind or ocean currents) so rays are convected and refracted by the flow; without it the medium is at rest. Material Discontinuity handles interior boundaries between media with different sound speeds using deterministic ray splitting (Snell refraction plus optional reflected secondary rays with automatic R and T), or represents a thin absorbing layer such as a curtain with user-defined reflection and transmission coefficients.
tools.usage: Right-click Ray Acoustics > Background Velocity (bvel1) / Material Discontinuity (matd1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rac").create("bvel1", "BackgroundVelocity", 3); create("matd1", "MaterialDiscontinuity", 2)

parameters.name: u (Background Velocity)
parameters.description: Velocity field components (m/s).

parameters.name: BoundaryProperties
parameters.description: NoLayer | AbsorbingLayer.

parameters.name: ReleaseReflectedRays, Ith, Qth
parameters.description: Always | Never | BasedOnLogicalExpression and intensity/power thresholds for secondary rays.

parameters.name: R, T
parameters.description: Reflection and transmission coefficients for the absorbing layer.

tools.notes: Secondary rays need extra degrees of freedom allocated at the interface level. Graded media (continuous c variation) require the 'graded media' intensity option.

tools.name: Receiver 3D / Receiver 2D (ray acoustics datasets)
tools.description: Results datasets that evaluate ray data from a Ray (dataset) at a receiver location defined by center and radius, either from a Receiver feature or from an expression-based radius (from the number of rays, room volume and source-receiver distance). They provide the input for the Impulse Response plot, including receiver directivity, interpolation between time steps and extra time-step rendering.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > More Datasets > Receiver 3D. Java: model.result().dataset().create("re1", "Receiver3D"); model.result().dataset("re1").set("data", "ray1")

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Source Ray dataset.

parameters.name: receiverselection / center, radius
parameters.description: Receiver feature or center and radius of the receiver sphere.

parameters.name: radiusinput, nrays, volume, distance
parameters.description: expr (radius from ray count, room volume and distance) | user.

parameters.name: directivity, directivityexpr
parameters.description: omnidirectional | user | userlinear receiver directivity.

parameters.name: interpolation, extrasteps
parameters.description: linear | cubic interpolation and rendering of extra time steps.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Use one Receiver dataset per receiver position.

tools.name: Impulse Response (ray acoustics plot)
tools.description: 1D plot that reconstructs the room impulse response at a receiver from ray arrival times and band powers of a Receiver dataset, combining octave, 1/3-octave or 1/6-octave band solutions (from a parametric sweep over the band center frequency) with filter kernels into a broadband or per-band response. It can show the time signal, its Fourier transform, levels in dB and randomized-phase reconstruction, and it hosts the Energy Decay subfeature for reverberation and clarity metrics.
tools.usage: Results > 1D Plot Group > Impulse Response (dataset: Receiver 3D). Java: model.result().create("pg1", "PlotGroup1D"); model.result("pg1").create("imp1", "ImpulseResponse"); model.result("pg1").feature("imp1").set("data", "re1")

parameters.name: freqtype
parameters.description: octave | octave3 | octave6 interpretation of the swept frequencies.

parameters.name: frequency, power, density, soundspeed, nrefl
parameters.description: Expressions for band frequency, ray power, medium data and reflection count.

parameters.name: advdisplay, filterkernel
parameters.description: broadband | indiband | filters display; brickwallkaiser or user-defined kernel.

parameters.name: transform, fouriershow, indb, dbtype
parameters.description: Fourier transform display and dB options.

parameters.name: randphase, sampfreq, zeropadding
parameters.description: Randomized phase, sampling frequency and zero padding.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. The plot also supports a function source for external IR data.

tools.name: Energy Decay (ray acoustics room metrics)
tools.description: Subfeature of the Impulse Response plot that computes and plots the Schroeder energy decay (or level decay or modulation transfer function) and tabulates standard room-acoustics metrics per band or broadband: reverberation times T20, T30 and T60, early decay time EDT, clarity C50 and C80, definition D50, center time Ts, first ray arrival time, apparent SNR and the speech transmission index STI. The start time can be detected automatically with a relative trigger threshold.
tools.usage: Right-click Impulse Response > Energy Decay (enyd1). Java: model.result("pg5").feature("imp1").create("enyd1", "EnergyDecay")

parameters.name: bandtype, bandfreq
parameters.description: indiband | broadband and the band frequency.

parameters.name: plot
parameters.description: energydecay | leveldecay | mtf.

parameters.name: t20, t30, t60, edt, c50, c80, definition, ts, tr, snr, sti
parameters.description: on/off switches for the tabulated metrics.

parameters.name: starttimemode, reltrigthreshold, starttime
parameters.description: auto | manual start of the decay evaluation.

parameters.name: tablelabel
parameters.description: Output table for the metrics.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Enough rays and a long enough simulation time (beyond the expected T60) are required for reliable late-decay metrics. The Acoustic Diffusion Equation provides statistical reverberation times as an alternative.

tools.name: Acoustic Diffusion Equation (ade)
tools.description: 3D energy-based room acoustics interface (energy finite elements, EFEM) that solves a diffusion equation for the acoustic energy density in coupled rooms with diffuse sound fields. It gives fast steady-state SPL distributions in buildings (Stationary study), energy decay curves and reverberation times (Time Dependent) and the decay modes of coupled room systems (Eigenvalue study, eigenvalues give T60 directly), with wall absorption, transmission loss between rooms, furniture (fitted domains) and air absorption per frequency band. Phase, direct sound and early reflections are not included.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Geometrical Acoustics > Acoustic Diffusion Equation; Studies: Stationary, Time Dependent or Eigenvalue. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ade", "AcousticDiffusionEquation", "geom1")

parameters.name: Band Input Type
parameters.description: Flat (continuous), Octave bands, 1/3 octave bands or User defined bands; Band Studied Nstudy.

parameters.name: Acoustic Diffusion Model (adm1)
parameters.description: rho, c, volume absorption m_a (or classical viscous/thermal at feval).

parameters.name: Room / Wall / Room Coupling / Point Source
parameters.description: Mean free path, absorption and exchange model, transmission loss and source power per band.

parameters.name: Sound Pressure Level Settings
parameters.description: Reference pressure for ade.Lp.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Postprocess ade.Lp (SPL) and the energy flux ade.Jx/Jy/Jz; statistical Sabine/Eyring variables are defined per room.

tools.name: Room and Acoustic Diffusion Model (Acoustic Diffusion Equation)
tools.description: Default domain nodes of the Acoustic Diffusion Equation. Acoustic Diffusion Model defines density, speed of sound and the volume (air) absorption coefficient, optionally the classical viscous and thermal absorption evaluated at a frequency or averaged over the studied band. Room defines each closed volume and its mean free path (ideal diffuse field 4V/S or user defined, e.g. from a ray-tracing computation) and provides statistical room-acoustics variables such as Sabine and Eyring reverberation times.
tools.usage: Acoustic Diffusion Equation > Acoustic Diffusion Model 1 (adm1) and Room 1 (room1, one per room). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ade").create("room2", "Room", 3); feature("room2").set("inputlambda", "IdealDiffuseField")

parameters.name: rho, c, m_a, feval
parameters.description: Density, speed of sound, volume absorption coefficient and evaluation frequency.

parameters.name: inputlambda, lambda
parameters.description: IdealDiffuseField | UserDefined mean free path.

parameters.name: mu, kcond, Cp, gamma
parameters.description: Fluid data for classical absorption.

tools.notes: Each room needs its own Room node with Wall subnodes for all its surfaces. Fitted Domain adds scattering and absorption by furniture (number density nf, cross section Qf, absorption alphaf).

tools.name: Wall (Acoustic Diffusion Equation)
tools.description: Subnode of Room defining wall absorption through the random-incidence absorption coefficient, entered as a single value (flat band) or per octave, third-octave or user band, optionally loaded from file. The exchange coefficient model sets how absorption enters the diffusion boundary condition: Sabine type (valid for alpha < 0.2), Eyring or Modified Eyring (valid up to alpha = 1), or a user-defined exchange coefficient.
tools.usage: Right-click Room > Wall (wall1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ade").feature("room1").create("wall2", "Wall", 2)

parameters.name: alpha / alphaN_o
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient (flat) or list per octave band.

parameters.name: exchange_model, h
parameters.description: Sabine | Eyring | Modified Eyring | user-defined exchange coefficient (m/s).

tools.notes: The random-incidence absorption differs from the normal-incidence value used in pressure acoustics impedance models. The exact exchange_model tokens are not listed in the completion data; set them in the GUI.

tools.name: Room Coupling / Mapped Room Coupling (Acoustic Diffusion Equation)
tools.description: Couple rooms so that acoustic energy flows back and forth through walls, doors or openings characterized by a transmission loss (single value or per band). Room Coupling acts on a shared interior boundary (Pair Room Coupling for assemblies) and can force continuity for large open connections; Mapped Room Coupling couples source and destination walls that do not share a boundary (e.g. when no mid-plane exists in the CAD) through a mapping.
tools.usage: Right-click Acoustic Diffusion Equation > Room Coupling (rctl1) / Mapped Room Coupling (mrctl1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ade").create("rctl1", "RoomCoupling", 2); create("mrctl1", "MappedRoomCoupling", 2)

parameters.name: TL / TLN_o / TLN_oto / TLN_ud
parameters.description: Transmission loss (dB), flat or per band.

parameters.name: bol_force_cont
parameters.description: Force continuity (zero transmission loss) for open connections.

parameters.name: Source/destination mapping (mapped version)
parameters.description: Orientation and mapping between the walls (advanced options).

tools.notes: Absorption properties of coupling surfaces must still be defined on the Room walls.

tools.name: Point Source / Domain Source / Fitted Domain (Acoustic Diffusion Equation)
tools.description: Sources and scattering regions of the Acoustic Diffusion Equation. Point Source injects a sound power qp (W) at a point, flat or per band, and may be time dependent for decay studies; Domain Source distributes a source power over a volume (e.g. a machine or HVAC unit); Fitted Domain represents furniture or equipment by its number density, average cross section and absorption coefficient, increasing diffusion and absorption in that region.
tools.usage: Right-click Acoustic Diffusion Equation > Point Source (ps1) / Domain Source (ds1) / Fitted Domain (fd1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ade").create("ps1", "PointSource", 0); create("ds1", "DomainSource", 3); create("fd1", "FittedDomain", 3)

parameters.name: qp / qpN_o
parameters.description: Point source power (W), flat or per band.

parameters.name: Q / QN_o
parameters.description: Domain source power.

parameters.name: nf, Qf, alphaf
parameters.description: Fitting number density (1/m^3), average cross section (m^2) and absorption coefficient.

tools.notes: Combine a Stationary step (steady state with the source on) followed by a Time Dependent step (source off) to get decay curves.

tools.name: Pair Acoustic-Structure Boundary
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling between Pressure Acoustics (frequency domain or transient) and Solid Mechanics across identity pairs of an assembly geometry, allowing nonconforming meshes at the fluid-structure interface. Because wave speeds differ strongly in solids and fluids, each side can be meshed to its own wavelength, saving degrees of freedom in large vibroacoustic models.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Pair Acoustic-Structure Boundary (asp1); create identity pairs (Form Assembly). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("asp1", "PairAcousticStructureBoundary", 2); multiphysics("asp1").set("pairs", new String[]{"ap1"})

parameters.name: Acoustics_physics, Structure_physics
parameters.description: Coupled pressure acoustics and structural interfaces.

parameters.name: Pair Selection (pairs)
parameters.description: Identity pairs where the coupling applies.

tools.notes: Type string and default tag prefix (asp) come from the COMSOL multiphysics plugin definition; the property names Acoustics_physics/Structure_physics follow the coupling types 'Acoustics,Structure'. The conforming-mesh version is Acoustic-Structure Boundary (asb).

tools.name: Thermoviscous Acoustic-Structure Boundary (and Pair version)
tools.description: Couples Thermoviscous Acoustics (frequency or time domain) to Solid Mechanics, Shell, Layered Shell, Membrane or Multibody Dynamics, enforcing continuity of the full velocity/displacement (no slip) or only its normal component (slip), with isothermal or adiabatic thermal condition, and transferring the total fluid stress (including viscous stresses) to the structure. It is the core coupling for condenser and MEMS microphones, micro-speakers and vibrating micromirrors; shells or membranes inside the fluid get an automatic slit. The Pair version works across nonconforming assembly pairs.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Thermoviscous Acoustic-Structure Boundary (tsb1) or Pair ... (tsp1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("tsb1", "ThermoacousticStructureBoundary", 2); create("tsp1", "PairThermoviscousAcousticStructureBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Thermoacoustics_physics, Structure_physics
parameters.description: Coupled interfaces (ta/tatd and solid/shell/mbrn/...).

parameters.name: MechanicalCondition
parameters.description: NoSlip | PerfectSlip.

parameters.name: ThermalCondition, ThermalConstraintType
parameters.description: Isothermal | Adiabatic and constraint type.

parameters.name: ConstraintType, ShowConstraintSettings
parameters.description: StudyControlled or explicit constraint settings.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Also used in mems_microphone_slip_wall, piezo_mems_speaker, loudspeaker_driver_transient and vibrating_micromirror.

tools.name: Thermoviscous Acoustic-Thermoelasticity / Thermal Perturbation Boundary
tools.description: Couplings that replace the ideal isothermal wall of thermoviscous acoustics by a real thermal interaction with the solid. Thermoviscous Acoustic-Thermoelasticity Boundary couples thermoviscous acoustics to Solid Mechanics plus Heat Transfer in Solids (thermoelasticity with Thermal Expansion), capturing combined mechanical and thermal interaction; Thermoviscous Acoustic-Thermal Perturbation Boundary couples only the temperature variation to a heat-transfer interface and must be combined with a mechanical wall condition. Relevant for MEMS and for fluid-solid pairs with similar thermal properties (water-glass).
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Thermoviscous Acoustic-Thermoelasticity Boundary (tatb1) / Thermal Perturbation Boundary (tatpb1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("tatb1", "ThermoviscousAcousticThermoelasticityBoundary", 2); create("tatpb1", "ThermoviscousAcousticThermalPerturbationBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Thermoacoustics_physics, Structure_physics, ThermalPerturbation_physics
parameters.description: Coupled ta/tatd, solid and ht interfaces.

parameters.name: MechanicalCondition (tatb)
parameters.description: NoSlip or slip.

parameters.name: ThermalConstraintType
parameters.description: Constraint type for the temperature continuity.

tools.notes: If the Adiabatic formulation is used in thermoviscous acoustics, no thermal coupling is performed.

tools.name: Thermoviscous Acoustic SLNS-Structure Boundary
tools.description: Couples the Thermoviscous Acoustics, SLNS Approximation interface to Solid Mechanics, Shell, Layered Shell, Membrane or Multibody Dynamics: the fluid load acts on the structure, the structural acceleration drives the fluid, and the boundary conditions of the viscous and thermal scaling functions are set on the interface. Thin interior shells or membranes get a pressure slit with proper up/down coupling. It enables efficient lossy vibroacoustic models of large microacoustic systems.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Thermoviscous Acoustic SLNS-Structure Boundary (tssb1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("tssb1", "ThermoviscousAcousticsSLNSStructureBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Acoustics_physics, Structure_physics
parameters.description: The slns interface and the structural interface.

tools.notes: Type string ThermoviscousAcousticsSLNSStructureBoundary and tag tssb come from the multiphysics plugin definition (coupling types Acoustics,Structure).

tools.name: Aeroacoustic-Structure Boundary
tools.description: Couples the Linearized Navier-Stokes interfaces (acoustics in a background flow with viscous and thermal losses) to Solid Mechanics, Shell, Layered Shell, Membrane or Multibody Dynamics, giving frequency-domain fluid-structure interaction with flow, e.g. flow-induced vibration damping of plates, flow meters or liners with flexible facings. As for the thermoviscous coupling, full (no slip) or normal-only displacement continuity and isothermal or adiabatic conditions can be chosen, and the stress is continuous across the boundary.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Aeroacoustic-Structure Boundary (aesb1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("aesb1", "AeroacousticStructureBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Aeroacoustic_physics, Structure_physics
parameters.description: Coupled lnsf/lnst interface and structure.

parameters.name: Mechanical condition
parameters.description: No slip (full displacement continuity) or slip (normal only).

parameters.name: Thermal condition
parameters.description: Isothermal or adiabatic.

tools.notes: Only the Linearized Navier-Stokes interfaces are supported (not linearized Euler or potential flow). Type string, tag aesb and coupling types Aeroacoustic,Structure were read from the multiphysics plugin definition; no Application Library model uses it, so property tokens for the conditions are unconfirmed.

tools.name: Acoustic-Thermoviscous Acoustic Boundary (and Pair version)
tools.description: Couples a Thermoviscous Acoustics domain to a Pressure Acoustics domain (FEM or BEM, frequency or time domain) so that the expensive thermoviscous model is only used near walls and in narrow regions while bulk regions use pressure acoustics; it enforces pressure/normal-stress and normal-velocity continuity assuming adiabatic behavior. Where the two domains meet a wall, set slip and adiabatic conditions locally on the thermoviscous side to stay physical. The Pair version supports nonconforming assembly meshes.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Acoustic-Thermoviscous Acoustic Boundary (atb1) / Pair ... (atp1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("atb1", "AcousticThermoacousticBoundary", 2); create("atp1", "PairAcousticThermoacousticBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Acoustics_physics
parameters.description: acpr, actd or pabe.

parameters.name: Thermoacoustics_physics
parameters.description: ta or tatd.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Also used in eigenmodes_air_bubble, nonlinear_slit_resonator and nonlinear_transfer_impedance.

tools.name: Acoustic-Acoustic Boundary
tools.description: Couples two scalar-pressure acoustics interfaces across a boundary: Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain, Pressure Acoustics, Boundary Elements and Thermoviscous Acoustics, SLNS Approximation, or two instances of the same interface (e.g. different meshes, discretizations or fluid models). An Impedance subfeature can add an interior (transfer) impedance between the two sides. With SLNS the interface is assumed adiabatic and ideal-slip.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Acoustic-Acoustic Boundary (aab1); optional subnode Impedance. Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("aab1", "AcousticAcousticBoundary", 2); multiphysics("aab1").create("imp1", "CouplingImpedance", 2)

parameters.name: Acoustics1_physics, Acoustics2_physics
parameters.description: The two coupled acoustics interfaces.

parameters.name: Impedance subfeature
parameters.description: Transfer impedance between the domains.

tools.notes: Type strings AcousticAcousticBoundary and CouplingImpedance and the coupling types Acoustics1,Acoustics2 are from the multiphysics plugin definition; the _physics property names follow the convention seen in Application Library models. For FEM-BEM coupling of acpr and pabe the dedicated Acoustic BEM-FEM Boundary also exists.

tools.name: Acoustic-Porous Boundary
tools.description: Couples Pressure Acoustics (FEM or BEM) to a Biot poroelastic domain of the Poroelastic Waves interface: the pore pressure equals the total fluid pressure, the fluid pressure loads the elastic skeleton, and the air experiences a normal acceleration from the skeleton and pore-fluid motion. Used for absorbers with elastic frames, particulate filters, headphone foams, sea-bed sediments and porous material characterization (impedance tube simulations).
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Acoustic-Porous Boundary (apb1); added automatically by the Acoustic-Poroelastic Waves Interaction interface. Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("apb1", "AcousticPorousBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Acoustics_physics
parameters.description: acpr (or pabe).

parameters.name: Porous_physics
parameters.description: pelw.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. The Acoustic-Solid-Poroelastic Waves Interaction interface adds apb, psb and asb together.

tools.name: Porous-Structure Boundary
tools.description: Couples a Biot poroelastic domain (Poroelastic Waves) to Solid Mechanics, Shell, Layered Shell, Membrane or Multibody Dynamics with displacement continuity. Coupling can be Perfect bonding (glued, full displacement continuity) or Imperfect bonding (normal direction only, e.g. a foam lying loosely on a plate). In 2D the out-of-plane thickness difference between structure and acoustics is rescaled automatically.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Porous-Structure Boundary (psb1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("psb1", "PorousStructureBoundary", 2); multiphysics("psb1").set("Coupling", "PerfectBonding")

parameters.name: Porous_physics, Structure_physics
parameters.description: pelw and the structural interface.

parameters.name: Coupling
parameters.description: PerfectBonding (default) | imperfect (normal-only) bonding.

tools.notes: Only PerfectBonding is confirmed as a token from a model; check the imperfect-bonding token in the GUI.

tools.name: Background Potential Flow Coupling
tools.description: Unidirectional global coupling that passes the mean flow computed by Compressible Potential Flow (velocity potential, density, derived velocity and speed of sound) to the Linearized Potential Flow interfaces as their background flow inputs. Unlike the Background Fluid Flow Coupling it does not map between meshes, so both models should be solved on the same mesh; it also works inside PML domains where the potential flow is solved.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Background Potential Flow Coupling (pfc1); Study 1 Stationary (cpf), Study 2 Frequency Domain (lpff). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("pfc1", "BackgroundPotentialFlowCoupling", -1)

parameters.name: PotentialFlowSource_physics
parameters.description: cpf.

parameters.name: PotentialFlowDestination_physics
parameters.description: lpff, lpft or lpfbm.

tools.notes: The plugin definition lists this coupling with 'global' entity dimension, hence -1 in create().

tools.name: Background Fluid Flow Coupling
tools.description: Unidirectional domain coupling that maps a stationary CFD solution (any Fluid Flow interface, including turbulent flows) or imported CGNS data (Imported Fluid Flow) onto the acoustics mesh of Linearized Navier-Stokes, Linearized Euler or Convected Wave Equation models. It is solved in the dedicated Mapping study, which maps pressure, velocity, temperature, density and optionally turbulent viscosity with light smoothing to avoid numerical noise entering the acoustic equations.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Background Fluid Flow Coupling (bffc1); Study > Mapping (solve only bffc, plus iff when importing). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("bffc1", "BackgroundFluidFlowCoupling", 3)

parameters.name: Source_physics, Destination_physics
parameters.description: spf/iff and lnsf/lnst/lef/let/cwe.

parameters.name: mapPressure, mapVelocity, mapTemperature, mapDensity, mapTurbulentViscosity
parameters.description: Which flow fields are mapped (eddy viscosity for turbulent attenuation in LNS).

parameters.name: smoothingMethod, delta_diff
parameters.description: Smoothing (e.g. IsotropicDiffusion) and its diffusivity.

parameters.name: useNoSlip, useSymmetry, use...Constraint
parameters.description: Wall/symmetry treatment and constraints on mapped fields.

tools.notes: Also used in generic_nacelle_liner, ultrasound_flow_meter_generic and flow_meter_piezoelectric_transducers. The eddy viscosity from RANS may overestimate attenuation.

tools.name: Aeroacoustic Flow Source Coupling
tools.description: Unidirectional 3D domain coupling from a scale-resolving CFD model (LES, DES or RANS SST-SAS) or imported CGNS data to the Aeroacoustic Flow Source feature of Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain, the hybrid CAA workflow for flow-induced noise (Lighthill analogy). It is solved with the Transient Mapping study to map the Lighthill stress tensor and other source terms to the acoustic mesh, followed by a Time to Frequency FFT and a Frequency Domain study of the acoustics.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Aeroacoustic Flow Source Coupling (afsc1); Studies: Transient Mapping, Time to Frequency FFT, Frequency Domain. Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("afsc1", "AeroacousticFlowSourceCoupling", 3)

parameters.name: Source_physics, Destination_physics
parameters.description: The flow interface (spf or iff) and acpr.

parameters.name: Domain/boundary selections
parameters.description: Must match the selections of the Aeroacoustic Flow Source feature.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module (CFD Module for LES/DES). Type string AeroacousticFlowSourceCoupling and coupling types Source,Destination from the multiphysics plugin definition; no Application Library model uses it in 6.4.

tools.name: Acoustic BEM-FEM Boundary
tools.description: Bidirectional coupling between Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain (FEM) and Pressure Acoustics, Boundary Elements (BEM) enforcing continuity of total pressure. FEM is used for interior domains, porous or lossy fluids and structures, while BEM models the open exterior exactly, acting as a perfect radiation condition and giving far-field values directly (e.g. vented loudspeaker cabinets, Bessel panels, transducers in an infinite baffle with Exclude Boundary).
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Acoustic BEM-FEM Boundary (abfb1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("abfb1", "AcousticBEMFEMBoundary", 2); multiphysics("abfb1").set("BEMAcoustics_physics", "pabe"); set("FEMAcoustics_physics", "acpr")

parameters.name: BEMAcoustics_physics, FEMAcoustics_physics
parameters.description: pabe and acpr.

parameters.name: Impedance subfeature (CouplingImpedance)
parameters.description: Optional transfer impedance at the coupling boundary.

tools.notes: BEM leads to dense matrices; use the iterative solver suggestions for BEM-FEM models. Note the user's guide text lists 'apb1' as the default name, but the plugin definition and models use abfb.

tools.name: Acoustic-Pipe Acoustic Connection
tools.description: Global coupling that connects the end point of a 1D Pipe Acoustics (frequency domain or transient) model to an inlet/outlet boundary of a 3D Pressure Acoustics model in quiescent conditions, so long duct networks can be reduced to 1D while bends, junctions or devices are modeled in 3D. Pressure and volume flow are matched between the point and the averaged boundary.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Acoustic-Pipe Acoustic Connection (apc1); select the 3D boundary and the pipe end point. Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("apc1", "AcousticPipeAcousticConnection", -1)

parameters.name: Acoustics_physics, Pipe_physics
parameters.description: acpr/actd and pafd/patd.

parameters.name: Boundary Selection, Acoustics / Point Selection, Pipe Acoustics
parameters.description: 3D inlet boundary and 1D pipe end point.

tools.notes: Only valid without background flow in the pipe. 3D only (plugin sdimtypes = threed). Also used in probe_tube_microphone (Pipe Flow Module library).

tools.name: Acoustic-Structure Boundary, Time Explicit (with Pair and Convected variants)
tools.description: Time-explicit (dG) acoustic-structure couplings between Elastic Waves, Time Explicit and a fluid interface: Acoustic-Structure Boundary, Time Explicit couples Pressure Acoustics or Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit; Convected Acoustic-Structure Boundary, Time Explicit couples the Convected Wave Equation (flow tangential to the wall, n.u0 = 0). The Pair versions act across assembly identity pairs and are preferred because they improve the performance of the explicit method. Typical uses are seismic waves at the ocean floor, immersion NDT and ultrasonic flowmeters with elastic pipe walls.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Acoustic-Structure Boundary, Time Explicit (asbte1) / Pair ... (aspte1) / Convected ... (csbte1) / Pair Convected ... (cspte1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("asbte1", "AcousticStructureBoundaryTimeExplicit", 1)

parameters.name: Acoustics_physics, Structure_physics
parameters.description: pate/nate/cwe and elte.

parameters.name: pairs, useProjectionBasedQuadrature
parameters.description: Identity pairs and quadrature option for the pair versions.

tools.notes: Type strings: AcousticStructureBoundaryTimeExplicit, PairAcousticStructureBoundaryTimeExplicit, ConvectedAcousticStructureBoundaryTimeExplicit, PairConvectedAcousticStructureBoundaryTimeExplicit (plugin definition).

tools.name: Acoustic Streaming Domain Coupling / Acoustic Streaming Boundary Coupling
tools.description: Pair of one-way couplings from a frequency-domain acoustic interface (Pressure Acoustics or Thermoviscous Acoustics) to a single-phase laminar flow interface that add the second-order time-averaged acoustic body force (domain coupling) and the boundary slip/stress source terms (boundary coupling) driving acoustic streaming. They are used for acoustofluidics, microfluidic pumps and particle manipulation; the domain coupling also defines the Lagrangian velocity (asdc1.u_lagx, asdc1.U_lag, including Stokes drift) for particle drag. Solved with the Frequency-Stationary or Frequency-Transient study.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Acoustic Streaming Domain Coupling (asdc1) and Acoustic Streaming Boundary Coupling (asbc1), or the predefined Acoustic Streaming multiphysics interfaces. Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("asdc1", "AcousticStreamingDomainCoupling", 2); create("asbc1", "AcousticStreamingBoundaryCoupling", 1)

parameters.name: Source_physics, Destination_physics
parameters.description: acpr or ta, and spf.

parameters.name: IncludeMaterialTerms, SourceForMaterialParameters, dmudT, dmudp
parameters.description: Include material-derivative terms with viscosity derivatives.

parameters.name: SubtractLagrangian (domain)
parameters.description: Lagrangian-velocity related option.

tools.notes: With pressure acoustics as source, use the Thermally conducting and viscous fluid model plus Thermoviscous Boundary Layer Impedance on walls; the domain coupling cannot be used on poroacoustic, narrow-region or anisotropic domains.

tools.name: Thermoviscous Boundary Layer Impedance (Acoustic-Structure Boundary subfeature)
tools.description: Subfeature of the Acoustic-Structure Boundary coupling that adds viscous and thermal boundary-layer losses (the BLI model) on vibrating fluid-structure interfaces of a pressure acoustics model. The structure velocity is applied to the fluid and the full traction including viscous stresses is applied to the solid, so microphone diaphragms, MEMS speakers and vibrating particles get thermoviscous damping at pressure-acoustics cost; only the thermal condition and fluid/wall properties are set.
tools.usage: Right-click Multiphysics > Acoustic-Structure Boundary (asb1) > Thermoviscous Boundary Layer Impedance (tvb1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics("asb1").create("tvb1", "CouplingThermoviscousBoundaryLayerImpedance", 2)

parameters.name: ThermalCondition, BacksideWallCondition
parameters.description: Isothermal | Adiabatic | TemperatureVariation | ThermallyConductiveWall and backside condition.

parameters.name: WallType, d, rho_w, Cp_w, kcond_w
parameters.description: Finite or infinite conductive wall data.

parameters.name: mu, kcond, Cp, gamma, c, rho
parameters.description: Fluid properties.

tools.notes: Not valid in extremely narrow gaps where boundary layers overlap; use Thermoviscous Acoustic-Structure Boundary there.

tools.name: Acoustic-Piezoelectric Interaction, Frequency Domain (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface for electro-mechanical-acoustic transducers that adds Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain, Solid Mechanics and Electrostatics together with the Acoustic-Structure Boundary and Piezoelectricity couplings. It solves the Helmholtz equation in the fluid, elastodynamics in solids and the piezoelectric constitutive relations (stress-charge or strain-charge) with the electric potential, for sonar and medical ultrasound transducers (tonpilz, piezo disks, matching layers) and their far-field radiation patterns and electrical impedance. A transient version (Acoustic-Piezoelectric Interaction, Transient) also exists.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Acoustics > Acoustic-Structure Interaction > Acoustic-Piezoelectric Interaction, Frequency Domain. Java: physics().create("acpr", "PressureAcoustics", "geom1"); physics().create("solid", "SolidMechanics", "geom1"); physics().create("es", "Electrostatics", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("asb1", "AcousticStructureBoundary", 2); multiphysics().create("pze1", "PiezoelectricEffect", 3)

parameters.name: Piezoelectric Material (solid)
parameters.description: Stress-charge (cE, eES, epsilonrS) or strain-charge data, polarization coordinate system.

parameters.name: Terminal / Ground (es)
parameters.description: Electrical excitation (voltage or charge) giving admittance and TVR/sensitivity.

parameters.name: Exterior Field Calculation / PML (acpr)
parameters.description: Far-field radiation and open-boundary treatment.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module (piezo material also available with the Structural Mechanics or MEMS Module). Use pabe with Acoustic BEM-FEM Boundary for large exterior domains (tonpilz_transducer_prestressed).

tools.name: Adaptive Frequency Sweep (acoustics)
tools.description: Predefined acoustics study (type FrequencyAdaptive) that uses asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE) to compute a finely resolved frequency response with far fewer full solves, ideal for sharp resonances of mufflers, Helmholtz resonators and loudspeaker enclosures. The AWE metric is physics controlled (from the AWE Expression feature) or user controlled (expressions such as an averaged SPL), with a relative tolerance (default 0.01). The Frequency Domain study offers the same via its awe option; Frequency Domain, Modal is the modal alternative.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies for Selected Physics > Adaptive Frequency Sweep. Java: model.study("std1").create("frawe", "FrequencyAdaptive")

parameters.name: plist, punit
parameters.description: Frequencies (a fine range) and unit.

parameters.name: awefunctype
parameters.description: physicscontrolled (default) | usercontrolled.

parameters.name: awefunc
parameters.description: User AWE expressions (global scalars).

parameters.name: rtol
parameters.description: Relative tolerance of the AWE.

tools.notes: For acoustics use the ISO preferred frequencies entry method (Range > Entry method, 1/1 to 1/24 octave, ISO 266) when third-octave results are needed. The awefunc expression assumes an Integration component coupling intop1 defined over the cavity; any smooth global response metric works.

tools.name: Mapping / Transient Mapping (aeroacoustics studies)
tools.description: Dedicated study steps that transfer flow data to the acoustics mesh. Mapping (type Mapping) uses a stationary solver to map a steady CFD solution or imported CGNS data through the Background Fluid Flow Coupling for linearized Euler/Navier-Stokes and convected wave models. Transient Mapping (type TransientMapping) maps time-resolved LES/DES/SST-SAS flow-source data (Lighthill stress tensor) through the Aeroacoustic Flow Source Coupling, prior to a Time to Frequency FFT.
tools.usage: Study > Mapping or Transient Mapping; in Physics and Variables Selection solve only the coupling (and Imported Fluid Flow when importing). Java: model.study("std2").create("mapp", "Mapping"); model.study("std3").create("tmapp", "TransientMapping")

parameters.name: notstudy (Source)
parameters.description: Study with the flow solution, or imported data.

parameters.name: Destination mesh
parameters.description: Acoustics mesh to map onto.

parameters.name: initialtime, mappingtimestep, rtol (Transient Mapping)
parameters.description: Start time, mapping time step and tolerance.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Mapping is also used in generic_nacelle_liner and the ultrasound flowmeter models.

tools.name: Frequency-Stationary / Frequency-Transient (acoustic streaming studies)
tools.description: Study steps with tailored solvers for acoustic streaming: the acoustic interface is solved in the frequency domain and the flow interface as stationary (Frequency-Stationary, type FrequencyStationary) or time dependent (Frequency-Transient, type FrequencyTransient) in the same step, with the streaming couplings evaluated as Frequency-stationary/transient. The transient variant re-evaluates the acoustics at every time step, valid when flow and heating evolve much slower than the acoustic period.
tools.usage: Study > Frequency-Stationary or Frequency-Transient (only with Acoustic Streaming Domain/Boundary Coupling). Java: model.study("std1").create("fstat", "FrequencyStationary"); model.study("std1").feature("fstat").set("freq", "f0")

parameters.name: freq
parameters.description: Acoustic driving frequency.

parameters.name: tlist, initialtime, rtol (Frequency-Transient)
parameters.description: Output times, initial time and tolerance.

parameters.name: usestol, stol (Frequency-Stationary)
parameters.description: Tolerance options.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module license.

tools.name: Octave Band (acoustics plot)
tools.description: 1D plot for frequency responses in octave, 1/3, 1/6 or 1/12 octave bands or as a continuous curve, with Z, A, C or user weighting (IEC 61672-1). Expression types amplitude, power, transfer (ratio of two quantities) or general, each with a reference, cover SPL, sensitivity, transmission loss and insertion loss curves; quantities can be band power, band-averaged PSD or continuous, drawn as bars, outlines or lines with optional moving average.
tools.usage: Results > 1D Plot Group > Octave Band. Java: model.result("pg2").create("oct1", "OctaveBand"); model.result("pg2").feature("oct1").set("expr", "acpr.Lp_t")

parameters.name: expr, exprtype
parameters.description: Expression and type amplitude | power | transfer | general.

parameters.description: References for dB conversion.

parameters.name: quantity, bandtype

parameters.name: weighting, weightexpr
parameters.description: z | a | c | expression.

parameters.name: type, movingaverage
parameters.description: bar | outline | line; moving average smoothing.

tools.name: Directivity (acoustics plot)
tools.description: 2D contour-style plot of the spatial response versus frequency and polar angle, as used in the loudspeaker industry: the expression (typically the exterior-field SPL acpr.efc1.Lp_pext) is evaluated on an evaluation circle (unit or user center/radius/normal/reference direction) for a number of angles. Options include normalization to a given angle or to the maximum, logarithmic or linear frequency axis, swapped axes, restricted angle range and filled or line contours.
tools.usage: Results > 2D Plot Group > Directivity (dataset: frequency sweep). Java: model.result().create("pg4", "PlotGroup2D"); model.result("pg4").create("dir1", "Directivity"); model.result("pg4").feature("dir1").set("expr", "acpr.efc1.Lp_pext")

parameters.description: Number of angles and angular restriction.

parameters.name: circle, center2/center3, radius, normal, refdir
parameters.description: Evaluation circle definition.

parameters.name: layout, frequencyscale, contourtype, levels
parameters.description: frequencyx | frequencyy, linear | logarithmic, filled | lines, contour levels.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. For a single-frequency polar/balloon plot use the Radiation Pattern plot (existing entry); its 3D version can compute the directivity index.

tools.name: Pressure acoustics postprocessing variables (acpr.p_t, acpr.Lp_t, intensity, dissipation)
tools.description: Predefined result variables of the pressure acoustics interfaces (prefix = interface tag, e.g. acpr): total and scattered pressure acpr.p_t, acpr.p_s, incident field acpr.p_i, sound pressure level acpr.Lp_t / acpr.Lp (dB re the SPL reference), local speed of sound and impedance acpr.c_c, acpr.rho_c, wave number acpr.k, time-averaged intensity acpr.Ix, Iy, Iz and acpr.I_mag, and dissipated power densities acpr.diss_visc, acpr.diss_therm, acpr.diss_tot. Feature variables include absorption coefficients of Impedance nodes (acpr.imp1.alpha_n, alpha_ran), exterior field pext/Lp_pext and radiated power acpr.efc1.P_rad.
tools.usage: Any Results expression, e.g. Surface plot of acpr.Lp_t, Line Integration of acpr.Ix*nx+acpr.Iy*ny+acpr.Iz*nz for sound power. Java: model.result("pg1").feature("surf1").set("expr", "acpr.Lp_t")

parameters.name: acpr.p_t / acpr.Lp_t
parameters.description: Total acoustic pressure and SPL (defaults of the Acoustic Pressure and SPL plots).

parameters.name: acpr.I_mag, acpr.Ix/Iy/Iz (Ir/Iz in axi)
parameters.description: Time-averaged intensity (frequency domain only); with a Background Pressure Field optional background/scattered intensities.

parameters.name: acpr.diss_tot (and _visc, _therm)
parameters.description: Dissipated power density for heating couplings (e.g. ultrasound heating).

parameters.name: acpr.imp1.alpha_n, acpr.imp1.alpha_ran
parameters.description: Normal- and random-incidence absorption coefficients on impedance boundaries.

parameters.name: acpr.efc1.pext, acpr.efc1.Lp_pext, acpr.efc1.P_rad
parameters.description: Exterior field pressure, SPL and radiated power.

tools.notes: The instantaneous intensity is not available in pressure acoustics transient (the velocity is not solved); interfaces solving for velocity (LE, LNS, thermoviscous) define instantaneous intensity (e.g. ta.v_inst). Analogous variables exist for other interfaces: pabe.Lp_t, lnsf.Lp_t, ade.Lp, pafd.Lp.

tools.name: Port, S-parameter and transmission-loss variables (Pressure Acoustics)
tools.description: Global variables generated by acoustic Port conditions for waveguide analysis: incident and outgoing port powers acpr.port1.P_in and acpr.portN.P_out, the scattering matrix acpr.S11, acpr.S21, ..., the port-to-port transmission loss acpr.TL_12 and, when the model has exactly two plane-wave ports, the two-port transfer matrix acpr.T11..T22 and impedance matrix acpr.Z11..Z22. Mode shapes and cut-off frequencies are available as acpr.port1.pn and acpr.port1.fc; lumped ports give acpr.lport1.p1/p2 and Lp1/Lp2. A port sweep (Activate port sweep with a PortName parameter sweep) builds the full S-matrix.
tools.usage: Results > Global Evaluation / 1D Global plot / Octave Band, e.g. 10*log10(acpr.port1.P_in/acpr.port2.P_out) or acpr.TL_12. Java: model.result().numerical().create("gev1", "EvalGlobal"); model.result().numerical("gev1").set("expr", new String[]{"acpr.TL_12"})

parameters.name: acpr.portN.P_in / P_out
parameters.description: Incident and outgoing power at port N.

parameters.name: acpr.Sij, acpr.TL_ij
parameters.description: Scattering coefficients and transmission loss from port i to j.

parameters.name: acpr.T11..T22, acpr.Z11..Z22
parameters.description: Transfer and impedance matrices (two plane-wave ports only).

parameters.name: acpr.portN.fc, acpr.portN.pn
parameters.description: Mode cut-off frequency and normalized mode shape.

tools.notes: Insertion loss is computed as the difference in radiated/received SPL or power between two model configurations (e.g. with and without a silencer) and plotted with an Octave Band transfer expression. Transfer/impedance matrices are only meaningful for plane-wave modes.

tools.name: Exclude Boundary (Pressure Acoustics, Boundary Elements)
tools.description: Removes selected boundaries from the boundary element problem so they neither contribute to BEM assembly nor to the solution. It is used when the BEM interface acts as an ideal infinite half-space above an infinite baffle coupled to a FEM pressure acoustics region: all BEM boundaries except those in the BEM-FEM coupling are excluded. This gives an exact radiation condition for baffled transducers and panels.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Boundary Elements > Exclude Boundary (eb1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pabe").create("eb1", "ExcludedBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Boundaries to exclude from the BEM problem.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Combine with the infinite-void / symmetry (infinite sound hard plane) settings of pabe for baffle problems.
